info.title: Tradewinds Age of Sail Economic API
info.description: Headless API for the Tradewinds 17th-18th Century Naval Trading & Financial Simulation

post.summary: Change player passphrase
post.description: Verifies the current passphrase, updates the player's Argon2id passphrase hash, and revokes existing API keys by default (`revoke_all_keys = true`).

400.description: New passphrase fails validation

post.summary: Create scoped API key
post.description: Mints a new scoped API key. Can be authenticated directly with `handle` + `passphrase` in the request body (allowing any scopes and company_id), or delegated via an `Authorization: Bearer` token holding the `account_manage` scope.

400.description: Invalid label, TTL, or empty scopes

401.description: Missing or invalid passphrase / Bearer token

403.description: Requires account_manage scope or attempts privilege escalation

get.description: Lists API keys owned by the authenticated player, optionally filtered by company_id. Company-bound keys can only list keys for their own company.

403.description: Cross-company key enumeration is forbidden

post.summary: Log in with handle and passphrase
post.description: Verifies the player's Argon2id passphrase and issues a revocable, optionally time-limited API key (defaults to 24h TTL and all scopes if omitted).

201.description: Authenticated and session API key issued

post.summary: Revoke API key
post.description: Immediately revokes an active API key. If `key_id` is omitted, revokes the calling Bearer token itself (self-revoke / logout). Revoking another `key_id` requires the `account_manage` scope.

403.description: Requires account_manage scope to revoke another key

post.summary: Revoke all API keys
post.description: Revokes all active API keys for the player (or for a specific company_id), optionally keeping the current calling Bearer key active.

403.description: Requires account_manage scope

get.description: Returns the authenticated player ID, optional bound company ID, granted scopes, and expiration timestamp for the Bearer token.

post.summary: Take a royal banking charter
post.description: Pays the 10,000 Cr charter fee to the Crown of your home region; you need 50,000 Cr of your own funds after it. Sets your rates on new demand and notice deposits (at most the Goldsmiths' lending rate), the notice, whether you take Crown deposit insurance (a daily premium), and optionally your exchange fee schedule (`exchange_fee_bps`, region to fee, 0-1200 bps each; a region left out is not offered). A bank lends and underwrites only while its vault cash stays at least 20% of its deposits.

409.description: Not enough capital, or already a bank

get.summary: Client terms you give (as a bank) or are given (as a client)
get.description: Every client's terms your bank has set, and every bank's terms for your company, newest change first. Nobody else sees them.

post.summary: Set your bank's terms for one client
post.description: Your bank's private terms for one company (with a deposit here or not): `rate_bonus_bps` (0-50) is added to the daily rate of every open deposit it holds with you, the sum capped at 50, from now on (interest already credited is untouched: its deposits are credited to now at the old rate first); `exchange_discount_bps` (0-1200) comes off your posted exchange fee on its withdrawals into another region, never below 0, fixed when each withdrawal is asked for. Send both `0` to clear them. Change them as often as you like. Only the bank and the client see them. Terms for a company of the same owner, or linked to yours, are allowed and flagged for review.

400.description: Out of range, or your own company

404.description: You hold no banking charter, or no such company

409.description: Your bank is winding down

post.summary: Deposit with a bank
post.description: Pays `amount_pence` from your vault in `banking_region` into the bank's, on demand or (`notice: true`) at its notice rate and notice. Interest is credited daily. Not with your own bank (`400`).

400.description: Your own bank

409.description: The bank is winding down

get.summary: Your deposits (or, for a bank, the deposits it holds)
get.description: Each deposit shows the rate it was opened at (`daily_rate_bps`), the bank's client terms for its depositor (`rate_bonus_bps`, `exchange_discount_bps`; `0` without any) and the rate interest is credited at now (`effective_rate_bps`, the two added, at most 50). Only the depositor and the bank see a deposit.

Every bank open or winding down, largest first: its deposit rates and notice, Crown deposit insurance, what it owes depositors, its vault reserves against the Crown requirement, what it has lent and locked underwriting, any withdrawals overdue, and its exchange fee schedule (`exchange_fee_bps`: the regions it pays withdrawals into besides a deposit's own, and its fee for each). A bank that cannot meet a withdrawal within a game day of it falling due fails.

post.summary: Change your bank's terms for new deposits
post.description: Same body as the charter. Rates, notice and insurance apply to new deposits only. `exchange_fee_bps`, when sent, replaces your exchange schedule at once for every withdrawal asked for from then on (a withdrawal already asked for keeps the fee it was quoted); change it as often as you like. Omitted, the schedule is unchanged.

post.summary: Wind your bank down
post.description: Stops taking deposits, lending and underwriting; from then on every game day each deposit securing a loan from the bank is first set off against that loan, then all the bank's cash is paid to its depositors pro rata as its loans come in. When nothing is left out, it closes, or, with depositors still unpaid, goes into receivership.

post.summary: Withdraw from a deposit
post.description: A demand deposit is paid at once as far as the bank's vaults reach (the rest stays owed and falls due now); a notice deposit is paid after its notice. Only the balance above withdrawals already asked for and any lock of a loan the deposit secures may be withdrawn. With `to_region`, it is paid into your vault in that region at the bank's exchange fee for it now (kept by the bank out of the amount, and fixed for this withdrawal however the bank reprices); a region the bank does not offer is refused (`409`). The bank pays the Crown's remittance fee itself on whatever it draws from a vault in another region. A bank that leaves a withdrawal unpaid a game day past due fails and winds down, paying its depositors pro rata.

400.description: More than you may withdraw

409.description: The bank is winding down, or does not offer exchange into `to_region`

get.summary: The bulletin: public deal talk, most recently active threads first
get.description: Public (no key needed). Threads with their title, the company that opened it, what it is about (`link`: an Exchange entry or a company), reply count and last post. A thread with no post for three real days is `archived`: readable, closed to replies. Taken-down titles read `removed by the harbourmaster` (or `deleted by its author`). Filter with `since` (a post after then); page with `cursor` (the previous page's `next_cursor`) and `limit` (default 30, max 100). Read a thread's posts with `GET /v1/bulletin/thread?id=`. Nothing said here is enforced: deals are gentlemen's agreements.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only threads with a post after this time.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page.

400.description: Bad cursor

post.summary: Delete your own bulletin post
post.description: Deletes your post within ten real minutes of posting; after that it is permanent (`409`). It keeps its place in the thread as `deleted by its author` and still counts against your hourly limit.

403.description: Not your post

409.description: Past the ten minutes, already deleted or removed

post.summary: Edit your own bulletin post
post.description: Replaces the `body` of your post (and, for a thread's opening post, optionally its `title`) within ten real minutes of posting; after that a post is permanent (`409`). Not announced again.

403.description: Not your post, or muted

409.description: Past the ten minutes, deleted or removed

post.summary: Flag a bulletin post for the harbourmaster
post.description: Asks the harbourmaster to look at a post (`reason`, 1-200 characters). Once per company and post (`409`); not your own (`400`). The harbourmaster decides by hand; flagging changes nothing by itself.

400.description: Your own post, or a bad reason

409.description: Already flagged by your company

post.summary: Reply to a bulletin thread
post.description: Replies to a thread (`body` 1-1,000 characters), signed with your company's name and announced to everyone (`bulletin_posted`). An archived thread (no post for three real days) or one the harbourmaster removed takes no replies (`409`). Counts against the 10 posts per real hour (`429 bulletin_limit`).

403.description: Muted by the harbourmaster

409.description: Archived or removed

get.summary: One bulletin thread with every post
get.description: Public (no key needed). The thread and its posts, oldest first, each signed with its company's name, with `editable_until` (its author may edit or delete it until then). A post taken down keeps its place and reads `removed by the harbourmaster` or `deleted by its author`.

post.summary: Open a bulletin thread
post.description: Opens a public thread: `title` (1-120 characters), the opening post's `body` (1-1,000), and optionally `link`: `{"type": "exchange", "kind", "id"}` (an open Exchange entry) or `{"type": "company", "name"}`. Signed with your company's name; announced to everyone (`bulletin_posted`). Limits per company and real hour: 10 posts, of which at most 3 new threads (`429 bulletin_limit`). A muted company gets `403 posting_muted`.

400.description: Empty or too long

403.description: Muted by the harbourmaster

404.description: The linked entry or company does not exist

post.summary: Incorporate a new trading company
post.description: Incorporates a new company at a Phase 1 port, provisions regional banking vaults with starter seed capital, and commissions a starter Hoy berthed with 8t of provisions. Call POST /v1/auth/create-key afterward with the new company_id to mint company-scoped API keys.

400.description: Invalid home port or name

409.description: Company name already taken or company limit reached

post.summary: Declare Admiralty Bankruptcy
post.description: Liquidates remaining company assets and obligations and issues a 250,000p Royal Bankruptcy Bailout Grant plus a fresh Hoy at the home port. Eligible when stranded (no ship, and liquid worth below the cheapest current rebuild quote of a starter hoy, at least 300,000p) or insolvent (liquid worth plus the forced-sale value of every hull beyond one starter hull below 250,000p). Liquid worth: cash in every regional vault (debt negative), escrow the receivership releases, and warehouse and ship cargo valued at the local NPC best bid. One receivership per player per 24 real hours; unpaid futures claims forfeit the grant.

200.description: Admiralty bankruptcy receivership completed and starter ship/bailout granted

409.description: Company is solvent, has ships at sea, or has active contracts/policies

post.summary: Dismiss a Resident Factor
post.description: Dismisses the company's Resident Factor at the specified port, freeing a factor slot and stopping daily salary upkeep.

get.description: Returns the ordered list of port IDs where the company currently maintains a hired Resident Factor.

200.description: List of ports with active Factors

post.summary: Hire a Resident Factor
post.description: Establishes a Resident Factor at the target port for a 75,000p setup fee (and daily salary upkeep). Up to 12 Resident Factors may be active per company.

403.description: Port phase locked

409.description: Maximum of 12 Resident Factors reached

get.description: Returns the company record, owner player handle, active fleet count, ports with hired Resident Factors, and regional banking vault balances.

post.summary: Move your home port
post.description: Makes `port_id` your company's home port. You need a Resident Factor there or a ship berthed or in its roadstead (`403 no_port_presence`); it must be an open port of an unlocked phase and not a smugglers' cove (`400`). Costs 2,500 Cr, paid from your vault in the new home's banking region to that region's Crown (`400 insufficient_funds` if it cannot pay). Once per real day (`409`; founding does not count). From then on your daily fleet and factor upkeep is billed in the new home's region, marques, patrols, R&D fees, licence deals and ship-share dividends are paid from your vault there, Goldsmiths' quotes default to it, and a receivership's Royal grant hoy is put there; bills already paid are unchanged and a chartered bank keeps its region. You are told (`home_port_relocated`); your public profile shows the new home.

400.description: A cove, your home already, or the vault cannot pay the fee

403.description: No factor or ship there, or the port's phase is locked

409.description: Moved less than a real day ago

get.description: Returns the company's preferences, with defaults for anything never set: `auto_remit_for_bills` (default true: a daily bill its region's vault cannot cover is topped up by ACH remittance, normal fee, from the other regional vaults, richest first, before the Crown Bailiff acts) and `auto_remit_min_reserve_pence` (default 0: auto-remittance never takes a source vault below this).

patch.description: Partial update: only the fields sent change; unknown fields and an empty body are rejected. Requires the `account_manage` scope, since settings are company-wide policy (auto-remittance moves money between regions on the company's behalf) that narrowly scoped bot keys should not change. Returns the full settings after the update.

400.description: No settings given, unknown field, or a value out of range

403.description: API key lacks the account_manage scope

post.summary: Accept a commission as its builder
post.description: Binds you to build an open commission: needs presence at the yard, escrows the commission's collateral from your vault in the yard's region, and leaves the deadline as posted. Deliver with POST /v1/contract/deliver-commission before it. Not your own commission (`400`).

403.description: No presence at the yard

409.description: Commission not open or lapsed

post.summary: Accept a P2P freight contract and load cargo
post.description: Binds the carrier company to an open freight contract, locks carrier collateral, loads the issuer's cargo onto the berthed ship, and sets a delivery deadline of twice the ship's laden sailing time over the route plus 2 game days.

200.description: Freight contract accepted and cargo loaded

post.summary: Accept a batch of up to 25 P2P freight contracts
post.description: Accepts between 1 and 25 open P2P freight contracts and loads their cargo onto the specified berthed ships. Atomic: if any item fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing item.

200.description: Batch of freight contracts accepted and cargo loaded

post.summary: Buy licence units from an offer
post.description: Takes `units` of a licence offer: 1..=what is left on a `per_unit` offer, exactly what is left on a `total` one. Paid from your vault in the offer's region (`licence.banking_region`, the holder's home region) straight to the holder (`licence_sale`); the units are yours at once (`GET /v1/rnd/licences`). Not your own company's offer; deals with your other or linked companies are allowed and flagged for review.

400.description: Bad units, your own offer, or insufficient funds

409.description: No longer open, or the seller no longer holds the patent

post.summary: Cancel one of your open charters
post.description: Withdraws an open charter your company posted: the reward for the undelivered tons is refunded to your vault (ledger reason `charter_cancelled_reward_refund`) and their reserved warehouse space freed. Deliveries already made stand. Announced as `charter_cancelled` where the charter was announced.

403.description: Not a charter your company posted

409.description: Not open

post.summary: Withdraw an unaccepted commission
post.description: Cancels one of your open (not yet accepted) commissions and refunds the escrowed price.

409.description: Commission already accepted or closed

post.summary: Withdraw a licence offer or request
post.description: Withdraws your open licence offer or request; a request's escrow for the units not filled is refunded. Units already sold stand.

409.description: No longer open

post.summary: Commission a hull to be built for you
post.description: Posts a commission: a ship of `ship_class` to be built at the shipyard `port_id` for `price_pence`, delivered within `deadline_game_hours` (6-1440). The price is escrowed now from your vault in the yard's banking region and must lie within 50%..=150% of the hull's rebuild value; `collateral_pence` (default 0, at most 25% of the price) is what the builder escrows on accepting, forfeited to you if it fails to deliver in time. You need no presence at the yard. Listed (`contract_type: commission`, `ship_class` on the listing) on the yard's quay. Withdraw it while open with POST /v1/contract/cancel-commission; if no one delivers by the deadline the price is refunded.

400.description: Price outside the band, bad deadline or collateral, or not a shipyard

403.description: Yard or ship class phase locked

post.summary: Post a P2P freight shipping contract
post.description: Locks physical cargo in the issuer's origin warehouse and escrows the freight reward in the regional margin account for a third-party carrier to haul.

post.summary: Offer licence units for your patent
post.description: The holder of a patent offers `units` (1-1,000) licence units for it: each lets the buyer make one component of the design at any yard. `price_basis` `per_unit` prices each unit (buyers take any number up to what is left) or `total` prices the whole lot (all-or-nothing). Nothing is escrowed. Public: listed in `GET /v1/contract/list?contract_type=licence_offer` (no port presence needed; `origin_port_id` is your home port, and the money moves in its region). Open `open_game_hours` (6-1,440, default 240), until taken in full, withdrawn (`POST /v1/contract/cancel-licence`) or the patent goes public.

400.description: Bad units, price or window

403.description: You don't hold this patent

post.summary: Ask for licence units for a patented design
post.description: Asks the holder of a patented design for `units` (1-1,000) licence units at `price_pence` (`per_unit`: the holder may fill any number up to what is left; `total`: the whole lot or nothing). The price for every unit asked is escrowed from your home-region vault (`licence_request_escrow`) and paid to the holder as it fills. Public: listed in `GET /v1/contract/list?contract_type=licence_request`. Open `open_game_hours` (6-1,440, default 240); withdrawing it, its lapse, or the patent going public refunds what is left (`licence_request_refund`).

400.description: Bad units, price or window, you hold the patent, or insufficient funds

409.description: The design isn't under patent (not granted, or public)

post.summary: Deliver cargo toward an Admiralty or Governor charter
post.description: Delivers physical cargo carried in from another port, from a ship berthed at or anchored in the roadstead of the charter port, toward an open charter: a Royal Charter or Governor Procurement Charter, earning pence and Crown Prestige (+1 per 1,000p of reward, accrued cumulatively), or a player charter (`funded_by: issuer`), paid from the issuer's escrow with the goods going into its warehouse there (no prestige). Player charters refuse deliveries from the issuer itself, other companies of its player and companies linked to it (403).

200.description: Charter delivery accepted; reward and Crown Prestige credited

400.description: Insufficient cargo or contract already completed

post.summary: Deliver a batch of up to 25 charter fulfillments
post.description: Delivers between 1 and 25 charter cargo installments in a single batch request. Atomic: if any delivery fails nothing is applied and the problem response's `batch_index` names the failing delivery.

400.description: Insufficient cargo or contract already completed

post.summary: Build and deliver a commissioned hull
post.description: Builds the commissioned hull at its yard, exactly as POST /v1/shipyard/build-ship would (`byom` from your warehouse there, or `turnkey_cash` bought off the yard's book, at your cost; quote it with GET /v1/shipyard/quote; turnkey here also passes over the buyer's and its siblings' asks), and hands the new ship straight to the buyer, berthed at the yard. The escrowed price is paid to you and your collateral released.

200.description: Hull built and delivered; price paid

400.description: Your own commission

409.description: Commission not accepted by you, lapsed, or the yard cannot supply a turnkey build

post.summary: Deliver a P2P freight contract at destination
post.description: Unloads contracted cargo from the carrier's ship (berthed or anchored in the destination roadstead) into the issuer's destination warehouse, releasing carrier collateral and paying the escrowed freight reward. If the issuer lacks free leased warehouse space the delivery is refused, the cargo stays aboard and the tender is recorded: should the contract then expire with the carrier still standing by, the issuer is in breach and the carrier is paid.

200.description: Freight cargo delivered; reward paid and collateral released

400.description: Insufficient cargo aboard

409.description: Ship not at the destination port, or issuer has insufficient warehouse space

post.summary: Fill a licence request for your patent
post.description: The holder of the design fills `units` of a licence request (1..=what is left on a `per_unit` request, exactly what is left on a `total` one): paid from the request's escrow into your vault in its region (`licence_sale`), and the requester holds the units at once.

400.description: Bad units

403.description: You don't hold this patent

409.description: No longer open

get.summary: List charters, freight contracts and commissions
get.description: Lists charters and P2P freight contracts filtered by type, port, destination, commodity, and status (default `open`), newest first; page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (1-200, default 50). Visibility: public charters (`is_public`: expansion and Admiralty) are listed to everyone, including unauthenticated callers. Other charters (governor procurement, crisis, guild, and player charters not posted `is_public`) are listed live only to companies with quay presence (a ship berthed or in the roadstead, or a Resident Factor) at the charter port; open freight only at its origin port and open commissions only at their yard; and your own contracts (freight you issued or carry, charters you posted or delivered to) always. Authenticated callers listing open contracts also get gossip copies of non-public charters elsewhere: news reaches your quay ports after 6 game hours plus the sea distance at 5 knots (~1 day across the Channel, ~6 days from the Baltic), and shows the charter as it was when the news left (`stale: true`, `gossip.news_as_of`, `gossip.heard_at_port_id`); it may since have been filled or lapsed. Delivery is first come, first served. Each row is the contract plus typed terms: `remaining_quantity` (tons still to deliver), and for charters `reward_per_ton_pence` (paid per ton delivered), `funded_by` (`crown`, `mint`, or `issuer` for a player charter, whose `issuer_company_id` posted it) and `title`; these are `null` for freight, whose `reward_pence` is paid whole on delivery. Commissions add `ship_class` (the hull ordered; `reward_pence` is the price). `expires_at` is when an open contract lapses.

post.summary: Post a charter: a request for goods delivered to your warehouse
post.description: Asks for `quantity` tons of `commodity_id` delivered at `port_id`, paying `reward_per_ton_pence` per ton (at most 10x the good's base price) to whoever delivers, in parts, cargo carried in from another port (`POST /v1/contract/deliver-charter`). The whole reward is escrowed from your vault in the port's banking region (ledger reason `charter_reward_escrow`) and every ton's room is reserved in your leased warehouse there, so you need that much free leased space at posting; the goods land in your warehouse as they arrive. What is left of the reward and the space comes back when the charter lapses (`duration_game_days`, default 10, clamped to 2..=20) or you cancel it. The issuing company itself cannot deliver. `is_public` lists it everywhere; otherwise it is seen live on the port's quay and spreads elsewhere as delayed coffee-house gossip, like a Crown charter (`charter_posted`). At most 10 open charters per company. Rewards far above the market are flagged to the Admiralty.

400.description: Reward above the cap, insufficient funds or free leased warehouse space

409.description: Too many open charters

post.summary: Buy an open envelope
post.description: Buys the envelope once and for all: needs presence at its posting port (storage tier or better: a warehouse lease, a ship there, or a Resident Factor). The price moves from your vault to the seller's in that port's banking region, the envelope closes (no resale) and its contents are returned here and kept under `GET /v1/envelope/mine`. Not your own envelope (`400`).

403.description: No presence at the posting port

409.description: Already sold, withdrawn or lapsed

get.summary: List sealed intelligence envelopes for sale
get.description: Public (no key needed): every open, unexpired envelope anywhere, newest first; filter by posting `port_id`, `category` (`port_reports`, `charters`, `sailings`) or `covers_port_id`, page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (1-200, default 50). Each listing shows where it was sealed (and where a buyer must have presence), a title generated from the contents (e.g. `London + Dover prices, 2 charters, 6h old`: the oldest item's age in game time), item counts per section, the ports covered, the oldest and newest item's timestamps and ages, and the price. Never the contents. The seller (`seller_company_id`, `seller_company_name`) is `null` unless you send a company key with quay presence at the posting port (you can already see who is there) or are the seller; a buyer sees it under `GET /v1/envelope/mine`.

parameters.name: port_id
parameters.description: Only envelopes posted at this port.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Only envelopes with this section.

parameters.name: covers_port_id
parameters.description: Only envelopes whose contents cover this port.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Return envelopes older than this id (the last id of the previous page).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, 1..=200).

get.description: Envelopes your company sealed (any status) and envelopes it bought, newest first, each with its full `contents` and your `role` (`seller` / `buyer`); filter with `role`, page with `cursor` and `limit` (1-200, default 50). A bought envelope's contents are yours to read from anywhere.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only envelopes on this side (default: both).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, 1..=200).

post.summary: Seal and list an intelligence envelope
post.description: Seals game data your company holds at `port_id` into an envelope and lists it at `price_pence`. Needs quay presence at the port (a ship berthed or in the roadstead, or a Resident Factor): the news must have physically reached it. The contents are copied verbatim, each item with its original timestamp (no free text): `port_reports` (the coffee-house board there plus your own crews' reports, including that port's quay as they saw it), `charters` (the port's own non-public charters, live, and the news of others' that has reached it) and `sailings` (the port's sailing notices of the last 24 game hours). Narrow the reports with `report_port_ids` and the reports and charters with `commodity_ids`. Lapses unsold after `expires_in_game_hours` (default 72, at most 240). At most 20 open envelopes per company.

403.description: No quay presence at the port

409.description: Nothing of a requested section is held there, or too many open envelopes

post.summary: Withdraw your unsold envelope
post.description: Takes your open (or lapsed) envelope off the market. Only the seller may withdraw it.

403.description: Not your envelope

409.description: Already sold or withdrawn

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Only deliver events of this `event_type`.

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description:
Resume after this event id (`0` replays the retained history first); omitted, the stream
delivers only events logged after it opens. Ignored when a `Last-Event-ID` header is sent.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume after this event id (sent automatically by EventSource on reconnect), or `0` to replay the retained history; takes precedence over `after_id`

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each visible StreamEvent is sent with `id:` = event id, `event:` = event_type, `data:` = StreamEvent JSON. Without `Last-Event-ID` or `after_id` only events logged after the stream opens are sent; `0` replays the retained history first. On resume, every visible event logged after `Last-Event-ID` is replayed from the event log (kept 7 days), then the stream goes live with no gaps or duplicates. Control events without an id: `gap` (StreamGap: the resume id is past retention or unknown, events may have been missed, resync via REST, the stream continues live), `auth_revoked` / `auth_expired` (StreamAuthEnded: the API key is no longer valid, the stream ends). Port-scoped events are delivered only for ports where the company has quay-tier visibility (a ship berthed/anchored there or a Resident Factor), at delivery time; the key is re-checked and quay ports refreshed every 30s; keep-alive comments are sent every 15s.

429.description: The company already has the maximum number of open streams (5)

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description:
Return events logged after this event id. `0` replays the retained history from the oldest
event; omitted, the poll starts at the newest event and returns only events logged after
the request.

200.description: Catch-up / long-poll batch of up to `limit` logged events after `after_id` (`after_id=0`: from the oldest retained event; omitted: only events logged after the request), in log order, filtered by company authorization and quay-tier port visibility (ship in port or Resident Factor) as of the request. Waits up to `timeout_ms` when none match. Page forward by passing the last returned id as `after_id`.

410.description: `after_id` is not in the event log (events are kept 7 days) or never existed; events may have been missed, resync via REST

get.summary: The Exchange: every open player offer, wherever it was posted
get.description: Public (no key needed). Every player-made offer open now, newest first: ships for sale (`ship_for_sale`: name, class, guns, fitted components, port, price), commissions not yet taken (`commission`: yard, class, price, deadline), ventures raising capital (`venture`: origin and destination, investors' share, raise deadline, capital raised so far; never their cargo), ship 64ths for sale (`ship_shares`: ship, class, 64ths, price per 64th), licence offers and requests (`licence_offer`, `licence_request`: design, units left, price and basis), loan requests (`loan_request`: borrower, principal, term, collateral kind and the borrower's loan record), open banks (`bank`: posted rates, notice and exchange fee schedule; dated by their last change of terms) and futures orders waiting for a counterparty (`futures`: hub, good, side, lot, strike, maturity). An entry leaves the board the moment its offer is sold, filled, taken, withdrawn or lapses. Ship listings, commissions and ventures posted `unlisted` stay on their port's quay only. Each entry carries its owner's `note` (plain words, no numbers), or `removed by the harbourmaster`. Acting on an entry keeps the offer's own rules: use its `id` with the offer's own endpoint (buying a ship still needs presence at its port). Filter by `kind`, `region` (banking region) and `since` (posted after); page with `cursor` (the previous page's `next_cursor`) and `limit` (default 50, max 200).

parameters.description: Only this kind of offer.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Only offers in this banking region.

parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page.

post.summary: Set the note on your Exchange entry
post.description: Sets (or, with an empty or `null` `note`, clears) the one note on an open Exchange entry of yours: plain text, at most 200 characters, and **no digits at all** (`400`): the entry already shows the offer's prices, sizes and dates, so a note carries words only. Only the offer's owner may (`403`); a note the harbourmaster removed cannot be changed (`409`); a company the harbourmaster muted cannot set notes (`403 posting_muted`).

400.description: Too long, or holds a digit

403.description: Not your offer, or muted

409.description: The note was removed by the harbourmaster

post.summary: Announce a convoy ahead of its sailing, before any ship commits
post.description: Schedules a convoy from `origin_port_id` to `dest_port_id` departing in `depart_in_game_minutes` (game time, 1 game hour to 14 game days) with no ship yet, on the same terms as `create-convoy` (`admission`, `visibility`, `min_speed_centiknots`, `escort_fee_pence_per_ton`). Ships, the organizer's own included, muster into it with `POST /v1/fleet/join-convoy` any time before it departs; a ship in a forming convoy waits in the roadstead (no docking, no sailing alone, its crew eats), so announce early and join late. A public announcement spreads as coffee-house news (`GET /v1/world/port` `convoy_notices`). Needs a presence at the origin (a ship, a Resident Factor or a warehouse lease); at most 5 announced convoys still forming per company, ships joined or not. One with no ship anchored at the origin when it is due is cancelled.

400.description: Bad terms or no route

403.description: No presence at the origin

409.description: Too many announced convoys still forming

post.summary: Approve a pending convoy join request
post.description: Organizer only, while forming: attaches the requesting ship (still anchored at the origin, not below the minimum speed).

403.description: Not the organizer

409.description: Convoy not forming, ship not ready at origin, or too slow

post.summary: Buy a listed ship
post.description: Buys a listed ship where it lies. Needs quay presence at its port (a ship in port or a Resident Factor). The price moves from your vault to the seller's in the port's banking region and the ship becomes yours at once, keeping its berth or roadstead place, stores and guns (its gossip from other ports is cleared); berth dues up to the sale are the seller's, yours from then on. Not your own ship (`400`); refused if the price has drifted outside 50%..=150% of the hull's rebuild value since listing (409: the seller must relist). A price outside 80%..=125% of the rebuild value is flagged for review.

403.description: No quay presence at the port

409.description: Listing not open, or the ship can no longer change hands

post.summary: Withdraw a ship from sale
post.description: Cancels one of your open ship listings.

409.description: Listing not open

get.description: Lists convoys the company may see (public ones, and private ones it organizes, was invited to or has a ship in), filtered by id, origin port or status, with route legs, members (hull class, cannons, escort flag, escort fee) and the voyage estimate. The organizer also sees pending join requests and invitees.

post.summary: Organize a new convoy
post.description: Schedules a multi-ship convoy from an anchored flagship's port to a destination port, departing in `depart_in_game_minutes` (game time, 1 game hour to 14 game days; the flagship waits in the roadstead throughout, so for a long muster prefer `POST /v1/fleet/announce-convoy` and join later), clearing any berth queue slot on the flagship. Sets who may join (`admission`: open, approval, invite_only), who is told (`visibility`: public, private), an optional minimum speed and an escort fee per ton of a paying joiner's hold.

409.description: Flagship is not anchored in roadstead or is already in a convoy

post.summary: Depart port on a solo voyage
post.description: Plots the shortest unlocked sea route to the destination port and sets sail immediately. Requires turnaround lock to have expired and the ship not to be attached to a convoy. Refused (409 `insufficient_provisions`) when the stores cannot feed the crew to port even without hazards, unless `allow_starvation`; sails but returns a `stores_below_safe` warning when they hold less than the route's `safe_provisions_tons`. Sailing from a berth settles its berth dues (`berth_dues_pence`, `berth_dues_debt_pence`).

409.description: Ship is in turnaround lock, attached to a convoy, or already at sea

post.summary: Detach a ship from a convoy
post.description: Detaches a ship from its convoy while in port, or withdraws its pending join request; any escort fee is refunded. Ships actively sailing at sea cannot detach mid-voyage.

409.description: Cannot detach ship while actively sailing at sea

post.summary: Dock an anchored ship at a port berth
post.description: Moves a ship from offshore roadstead into a physical berth (or queues it if all of the port's effective berths are occupied within their protected window). Berthing is free, but berth dues accrue per game day berthed (`berth_dues_per_day_pence`, rising with occupancy; at least 6 game hours a stay) and are settled from the owner's vault in the port's banking region when the ship leaves the berth (offshore, depart, eviction) and daily in the upkeep pass; dues a vault cannot cover are booked as vault debt (collected by the bailiff). The roadstead is free. Ships attached to a convoy must detach first.

409.description: Ship is attached to a convoy, at sea, or not in roadstead

post.summary: Fund a Crown Naval Patrol in a sea zone
post.description: Suppresses `suppressed_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) of a sea zone's piracy for `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440), paying the Crown the zone's patrol price per bps per game day of the term (at least 100 Crowns) from the home regional vault, exactly as `GET /v1/fleet/patrol-quote` quotes it and fixed for the term; `cost_pence` in the response is what was paid. The price is never under 2 Crowns per bps per game day and rises with the zone's recent smuggling traffic. Contributions from every company stack, capped at 5,000 bps per zone. Patrols search ships carrying contraband through the zone; while it is in force the sponsor earns prize money from every smuggler seized there: the prize court pays half the seized ship and cargo's base value, split among the patrols in force pro rata by bps, less the Admiral's tenth, from the world mint into the vault of the region the patrol was paid from (ledger reason `patrol_prize`, a private `patrol_prize_paid` event naming the patrol, zone and amount, never the ship or its owner; `prize_earned_pence` accrues on the patrol). The sponsor is anonymous: the public `naval_patrol_funded` notice and `GET /v1/world/zones` show only the zone's totals.

400.description: Insufficient funds

post.summary: Invite a company to a forming convoy
post.description: Organizer only: the invited company's ships join without approval (even an invite-only convoy) and it sees the convoy if private.

403.description: Not the organizer

post.summary: Sponsor a Letter of Marque in a sea zone
post.description: Adds `added_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) to a sea zone's piracy for `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440), paying the Crown the zone's marque price per bps per game day of the term (at least 100 Crowns) from the home regional vault, exactly as `GET /v1/fleet/marque-quote` quotes it and fixed for the term; `cost_pence` is what was paid and `pricing` the quote it was charged at. The price is 60% of the prize money a bps-day of marque is expected to earn after the Admiral's tenth from the zone's player traffic over the last 7 game days, never under 0.1 Crowns per bps per game day. Contributions from every company stack, capped at 5,000 bps per zone. While it is in force the sponsor earns prize money from every pirate interception in the zone: the prize court pays half the seized cargo's base value, times the marques' share of the zone's piracy (marque bps over base + marque bps, patrols ignored), split among the marques in force pro rata by bps, less the Admiral's tenth (the Crown keeps a tenth of each sponsor's share: it is not minted), from the world mint into the vault of the region the bounty was paid from (ledger reason `letter_of_marque_prize`, a private `marque_prize_paid` event naming the marque, zone, amount, `admirals_tenth_pence` and goods, never the ship or its owner). The sponsor is anonymous: the public `letter_of_marque_issued` notice and `GET /v1/world/zones` show only the zone's totals, and the victim's events never name it.

201.description: Letter of Marque issued to privateers, with the quote it was charged at

400.description: Insufficient funds

post.summary: Join a forming convoy
post.description: Asks to put a ship anchored at the convoy's origin port into a forming convoy (optionally as an escort, if it mounts cannons). It joins at once (`joined`) if the convoy is open, the company is invited or organizes it; on an approval convoy it waits (`pending`) for the organizer. Any escort fee is escrowed now.

403.description: Convoy admits invited companies only

409.description: Convoy already departed, ship not anchored at origin, already in a convoy, or would hold the convoy below its minimum speed

post.description: Organizer only, before departure: detaches the ship and refunds its escort fee.

403.description: Not the organizer

409.description: Convoy not forming, or the ship is the organizer's own

post.summary: Offer one of your ships for sale where it lies
post.description: Lists a ship berthed or anchored in a port's roadstead for sale at a fixed `price_pence`, which must lie within 50%..=150% of the hull's rebuild value (`rebuild_value_pence` on the listing: what the Crown yard would charge to build it now, guns included). The ship must be free to change hands: no cargo (sealed freight and carried salvage included), outside any convoy with no convoy request open, and no open or bound marine insurance policy. Its stores and guns go with it (the listing records them, and the name and class, as listed); its gossip from other ports does not. Announced on the port's quay (`ship_listed`). The listing lapses (`cancel_reason: ship_moved`) if the ship sails, sinks, is seized, joins a convoy, changes its guns, has stores taken off or changes hands any other way.

400.description: Price outside the band of the rebuild value

409.description: Ship not at a port, in a convoy, carrying cargo, insured, or already listed

get.description: Quotes what `POST /v1/fleet/issue-marque` would charge now for `added_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) over `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440) in `sea_zone_id`, and why: the zone's player traffic over the last `window_game_days` (7) game days (`laden_passages`, `laden_passages_per_day`, `avg_cargo_base_value_pence`), `marque_bps_in_force` (every unexpired marque, corsairs too, that it would share each prize pool with pro rata by bps), `expected_net_prize_per_bps_day_pence` (prize money a bps-day of this marque is expected to earn there after the Admiral's tenth and that sharing, if the traffic holds, at the zone's piracy with it in force and its patrols), `price_per_bps_day_pence` (60% of that, rounded up, never under 10 pence; `floor_applied` when the floor set it), `cost_pence` (at least 100 Crowns) and `expected_net_prize_pence` over the term. A dead zone shows no traffic and the floor price. The price moves with traffic until you issue; then it is fixed.

post.description: Vacates a physical port berth (once turnaround lock has elapsed) or cancels a berth queue reservation, anchoring the vessel in the offshore roadstead. 409.description: Ship is still inside its physical turnaround lock or at sea

get.description: Quotes what `POST /v1/fleet/fund-patrol` would charge now for `suppressed_piracy_bps` (clamped to 50..=1500) over `duration_game_hours` (default 60, clamped to 5..=1440) in `sea_zone_id`: the zone's `price_per_bps_day_pence` (never under 2 Crowns; higher where smugglers have lately been sailing) and `cost_pence` (at least 100 Crowns). The price moves with traffic until you fund; then it is fixed.

get.description: Returns the Crown Naval Patrols the authenticated company funded (active and historical), newest first. Sponsors are anonymous: other companies' patrols are never listed; each zone's live totals are public at `GET /v1/world/zones`.

post.description: Moves provisions into the ship's stores, which its crew eats (per leg at sea, and in port at half the sea rate, a ton per 200 crew-days: `port_provisions_tons_per_day` on GET /v1/world/route): from its own cargo (`source: cargo`, berthed or in the roadstead; sealed freight is never touched) or from the company's warehouse at the berth (`source: warehouse`; needs free cargo space, since stores take hold space, and extends the stevedore turnaround). To buy provisions straight into the stores, place an IOC bid with `into_stores: true` on POST /v1/market/order.

403.description: Ship not berthed (warehouse) or not at port (cargo)

Any other hull is refused with `400`: merchant ships always share.

400.description: Not a packet

404.description: Ship not found or not yours

409.description: Ship is lost

The response adds Lloyd's posted price for the voyage as written (`lloyds_premium_bps`, as `GET /v1/insurance/quote` gives it; `null` if Lloyd's would not write it) and `above_lloyds_price` when `premium_bps` is above it: information only, the premium offered stands and nothing is refunded.

400.description: Invalid premium bps, ship not in port, or insufficient funds

get.description: Lists marine insurance policies across all ports, newest first. Page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen) and `limit` (1-200, default 50). Each policy still open for underwriting also carries Lloyd's estimate of the voyage: `lloyds_expected_loss_bps` (an upper bound on the expected claim, bps of the sum insured), `premium_margin_bps` (`premium_bps` minus it: an underwriter's expected margin is at least this) and `lloyds_min_premium_bps` (the premium Lloyd's writes at, once players have had their hour); all three are `null` on other policies.

Each group has the `collateral_locked_pence` and `open_policies` it holds now, and its results this season (`all_time`) and over the last `days` game days (`recent`; `1..=360`, default 30): `policies_written`, `underwriters`, policies settled safe / claimed loss / voided and with any claim, `cover_pence` (collateral locked on them), `premiums_earned_pence`, `claims_paid_pence`, `net_pence`, `loss_ratio_bps` and `return_on_cover_bps`. Results are booked on settled policies, with every premium and claim of their slices, from the ledger.

get.summary: Lloyd's posted price for a voyage policy
get.description: Quotes Lloyd's Coffee House Syndicate's posted price for insuring your ship (in port, berthed or anchored) from its port to `dest_port_id` for `insured_value_pence`, as if the policy were written now: `lloyds_expected_loss_bps` / `_pence` (Lloyd's estimate of the expected claim, an **upper bound**: legs summed, rescues undercounted) and `lloyds_premium_bps` / `_pence` (its posted price, 2.5x the estimate + 25 bps, or 1.75x the estimate + 25 bps when the hull is rated for the water of every leg). The quote is rated exactly as Lloyd's rates the policy before writing it (the same hull value, guns, convoy consorts in `priced_consort_ship_ids`, zone piracy and season), on the policy's full 15 days to expiry. Lloyd's looks at a policy an hour or more after it is written, with less time to expiry (so no harsher a season ahead), so while zone piracy, the ship's guns and its convoy stand as quoted the quote is an upper bound on the hurdle it then applies: a policy offering the quote is written; one below it may be too, and one a bp below the hurdle `GET /v1/insurance/list` shows (`lloyds_min_premium_bps`) never is. Lloyd's writes within its collateral caps. Offer less to attract player underwriters in that hour, who see the same estimate on `GET /v1/insurance/list`; Lloyd's writes at the premium you offer and refunds nothing above its price. The price moves with marques, patrols, the season and your convoy. `lloyds_writes` is false when the price is above the 3,000 bps maximum premium. Errors as `insurance/create`: `exceeds_insurable_value` above hull plus cargo aboard.

parameters.description: Your ship, in port (berthed or anchored) at the voyage's origin.

parameters.name: insured_value_pence

post.summary: Take a Goldsmiths' quote
post.description: Takes a Goldsmiths' quote before it expires: the ship goes under the house's lien (it may still sail, but cannot be sold, listed or transferred until you repay) and the principal is paid into your vault in the quote's region. The loan then runs as any other. Refused for a real day after you or one of your own or linked companies walked away from any loan (403 `goldsmiths_walk_away_ban`).

403.description: `goldsmiths_walk_away_ban`: you or a linked company walked away from a loan within the last real day

409.description: The quote expired or was taken, the ship is no longer pledgeable, or the house cannot lend that much now

post.summary: Approve a quote on your request
post.description: Takes the loan the quote offers: the pledged ship goes under the lender's lien (it may still sail, but cannot be sold, listed or transferred until you repay), pledged goods are locked in your warehouse, or the receivable is assigned, and the principal is paid into your vault in the request's region. Every other quote is released and the request closes. Interest accrues daily at the fixed rate; an amortised loan's installments are collected from your vaults as they fall due (a missed one has a game day's grace, then the whole loan defaults); at maturity whatever is owed is collected, and what cannot be is a default: the collateral is seized and the rest (with recourse) is a claim collected from your income and shown on your credit record. You may instead walk away (POST /v1/loan/default). Borrowing never helps you qualify for bankruptcy.

404.description: No such quote on your requests

409.description: The request or quote is not open, or the pledge is no longer free

get.description: Public credit record of `company_id`: what it owes on loans now (active and defaulted), how many it repaid, defaulted on and had written off, its open futures default claims, what it has lent out, whether it went through receivership, and its smuggling convictions (ships the Crown seized from it). Lenders price risk from it.

post.summary: Walk away from a loan
post.description: Defaults on a loan you owe by choice, active or already defaulted: an active loan defaults now and the lender takes its collateral as at any default (a pledged ship at sea or otherwise unable to change hands is seized once it can; it is under arrest meanwhile). Whatever the collateral does not cover is then written off for good, recourse or not: nothing more is collected from your income, and you keep your cash. A Goldsmiths' instant loan (not a ship mortgage) settles at no more than a yard would pay, at any default: the house takes the ship credited at its break-up value (35% of its rebuild value, no surplus paid back) and whatever is still owed above that stays a claim, collected from your vaults once the ship is taken or lost. After any walk-away the Goldsmiths lend nothing to you or your own or linked companies for one real day. The walk-away is permanent on your public credit record (`GET /v1/loan/credit`: `loans_walked_away`, `loan_walked_away_pence`) and shown to lenders on every loan request you post (`borrower_record`). It still counts as borrowing for bankruptcy eligibility. Without this call, a loan you cannot pay defaults and its shortfall stays a claim on you.

200.description: Defaulted; the shortfall is extinguished once the collateral is taken

409.description: Nothing owed, or already walked away from

get.description: Loans you made (`role=lender`) or owe (`role=borrower`), or both, newest first: active loans (with their fixed `annual_rate_bps`, the quote's `total_repayable_pence`, interest accrued so far, `owed_pence`, and the next payment due: `next_payment_due_at`, `next_payment_pence`, any `arrears_pence`), and closed ones. Page with `cursor` (the last `id` seen).

parameters.name: role

The principal is escrowed from your vault in the request's region until the borrower approves this quote (it becomes the loan) or another, you withdraw it, or the request expires. Not on your own company's request (`400`). A request secured by a deposit may be quoted only by the bank holding it (`403`), and only while the deposit's free balance covers this quote's total repayable (`409`).

For the term only your company may buy the good from the Crown merchants at the region's ports (your other companies and linked companies included in the bar), and only your resting bids are filled by the Crown's ladder; a non-holder's IOC buy that only the monopoly kept from filling is refused (409) naming you, and its turnkey ship builds needing the good are refused. post.summary: Offer a ship for passengers
post.description: Offers your ship lying in port (berthed or in the roadstead) to passengers for `dest_port_id` at `fare_per_head_pence`, taking at most `max_berths` heads in all (1-10,000). The groups waiting there for that destination choose among the offers every game hour (see `GET /v1/passengers/waiting`). A group boards only if the ship has free hold for all of it: a passenger takes a ton of hold, two to the ton in a packet, and passengers aboard leave that much less room for cargo, stores and freight. The offer stays open until you cancel it, or until the ship sails, changes hands or is lost; passengers already aboard stay aboard. One open offer per ship and destination (`409`). On boarding a group is promised an arrival (`GET /v1/passengers/aboard`); its fare is paid into your vault in the destination's region when the ship arrives there, less a share for every game day late, down to a floor. A ship that calls elsewhere first keeps them aboard; long overdue, they go ashore unpaid. If the ship is sunk, taken or seized, or changes hands, they are lost unpaid; Lloyd's does not insure fares.

What a group will pay is never shown: post an offer and see whether it is taken. Every game hour each waiting group looks at the open offers at its port for its destination, ignores any above what it will pay or on a ship without hold for the whole group, and boards the one with the lowest fare plus the cost of its time at sea (a faster ship may ask more and still win); ties go to the earlier offer.

post.summary: Sell a ship to the yard to be broken up
post.description: The buyer of last resort: the yard where the ship lies (berthed or in the roadstead, at a port with an open shipyard) buys it for 35% of its rebuild value (its class at the yards' current prices, plus its guns and fitted components; `rebuild_value_pence` and `payout_pence` in the result), paid by the Crown of the port's banking region into your vault there (ledger reason `shipyard_break_up_payout`). The ship is destroyed: its guns, components and stores go with the hull, nothing returns to the yard's stock, and its berth passes to the next ship queued (berth dues up to now are yours, `berth_dues_pence`). It must be free to change hands as for a sale (empty hold, no sealed freight or carried salvage, no convoy or convoy request, no open or bound insurance, no lien) and besides carry no passengers or open sailing offers, have no open sale listing, no shares held by other companies or 64ths listed for sale, and no open venture. Refused (409) while that region's Crown treasury cannot cover the payment. A sale to another company (`POST /v1/fleet/list-ship`, at least 50% of the rebuild value) always pays more when a buyer exists. Your last ship may be broken up. You are told (`ship_broken_up`).

post.summary: Commission a new ship at a shipyard
post.description: Constructs a new vessel at a shipyard port, paid from your vault in the port's banking region: Bring-Your-Own-Materials (`byom`, consuming the hull's materials from your warehouse there) plus labour, or `turnkey_cash`: the yard buys every material off the port's ask book for you (each fill settled as a market buy: player sellers are paid like any trade and you pay importer customs), adding the 15% yard markup on what it bought from the NPC ladder. At the discount yards (Lisbon, Boston, Havana) labour costs 30% less and there is no markup. The price is exactly GET /v1/shipyard/quote's while the book has not moved. `mortgage: true` has the Goldsmiths' Company of the yard's region pay 60% of the price (80% for an oceanic hull) as a ship mortgage (an amortised 180-game-day loan at the Goldsmiths' rate, with a lien on the new ship and recourse; returned as `mortgage`), so you need only the rest; one mortgage at a time (409 while you owe on one). Build and mortgage succeed or fail together.

409.description: The ask book cannot supply a turnkey material, or you already owe on a ship mortgage

The ship must have that slot free and no open marine insurance (its value changes). The yard charges 4% of the ship's rebuild value (`component_fitting_fee`), and the component's worth and the fee are added to the ship's rebuild value (sales, insurance, loans, shares). `GET /v1/fleet/ship` lists a ship's `components`.

get.summary: Quote the exact cost of a ship build

Per material: `cost_pence` (paid to the sellers), `npc_cost_pence`, `player_tons`/`npc_tons`, `customs_pence`, and `in_stock` (turnkey: the book covers it; BYOM: your unlocked warehouse stock here). `available` says whether the build can go ahead; `total_cost_pence` is null when a turnkey material cannot be supplied. `mortgage` shows what a ship mortgage would lend on the build (60% of `total_cost_pence`, 80% for an oceanic hull), its rate, installments and total repayable, and whether you may take one now. Departing before it completes cancels it (`underworld_run_cancelled`); the goods stay aboard. A ship lying in port with contraband aboard may be searched; if caught, the ship and everything aboard are forfeit.

By default only events still in effect; `include_expired=true` returns the world's full history (never pruned). Filter by `event_type`, `structural`, `port_id` and `since` (start time); page with `cursor` (the last id of the previous page) and `limit` (default 50, max 200). get.summary: Theatre progression: expansion tier progress and contribution leaderboards
get.description: Returns the world's `unlocked_phase`, the Admiralty expansion tier now open (each open charter's tons required/delivered/remaining, progress, current rate, escalations, `expires_at` and game hours left; the tier's tons delivered and remaining and its completion bonus pool) and every completed tier. Each tier lists its contributors by company name with the tons they delivered and their share of the tier's value delivered (`share_bps`, tons at the tier's base rates). The completion bonus is not split by `share_bps`: it goes to players with diminishing returns, each player's part in proportion to the square root of its value delivered across all its companies, so a large contributor's bonus share is smaller than its `share_bps`. Public: no company ids, balances or payouts.

get.summary: Hall of fame: past seasons' top players
get.description: Every ended season, newest first, with its top 10 players by final rank (each player ranked by their best company: `company_name`, `home_port_id`, `net_worth_pence`) and the cosmetic `title` the top 3 earned (`Season <n> Champion`, `Season <n> Master Mariner`). The archive survives world wipes; titles show on the winner's flagship company in later seasons and have no gameplay effect.

get.summary: Season leaderboard: top 20 players by net worth, and top 20 by growth this week
get.description: The live season leaderboard, recomputed every real hour (`refreshed_at`, `next_refresh_at`), never per request. Players rank by their **best** company only: one entry per player, naming that company (`company_name`, `home_port_id`), its `net_worth_pence` (cash and escrow in every region, goods owned at catalog base prices, hulls afloat at build value: the same figure the season archive records) and any hall-of-fame `titles` its owner won in past seasons. A company that went through Admiralty bankruptcy never ranks again; its player's other or new companies can. Top 20 only, no player handles or ids; marque and patrol sponsorship is never shown. With a company key, `you` is your player's own rank (also outside the top 20) and which of your companies holds it. `rising` is a second board, recomputed in the same hourly refresh: players ranked by how much their wealth grew over the last seven real days (`growth_bps`, and `gained_pence`), summed across all their companies so moving money between them is not growth. Growth is measured against what the player had at `window_start_at` (seven days ago, or their first hourly snapshot if later), or against 100,000 Cr if they had less. The same players can rank as on the main board, each shown under the same company; a player appears once they have a snapshot from an earlier refresh. With a company key, `rising.you` is your own place on it.

While a monopoly is in force only its holder (`holder_company_id`, `holder_company_name`) may buy the good from the Crown merchants' asks at the region's ports, and only the holder's resting bids are filled by the Crown's ladder in the port tick: everyone else buys it from the holder's (or other traders') resting asks. Selling to the Crown is unaffected.

Says who holds it now (`held_by`) and whether it can be bought (`available`, with `unavailable_reason`: held, an excluded good (provisions, silver bullion), no market in the region, or, for an authenticated caller, the regrant cooldown: a player whose company, or a company linked to one of its companies, held the scope may not have it again until 10 game days after that grant ended, or the per-player cap). With a company key it also gives `player_monopolies_held` (grants in force held by your player's companies and companies linked to them), `max_monopolies_per_player` (2) and `player_cap_reached`.

get.summary: Get port details, your visibility tier, and Coffee House gossip board

get.summary: List ports with optional phase and banking region filters

get.summary: Plan shortest maritime route between two ports
get.description: Computes the shortest sea-zone path between two ports within `max_phase` (default: the world's current `unlocked_phase`), returning individual route legs, total distance in nautical miles, and the provisions the stores need: crews eat exactly one ton per 100 crew-days at sea and stores are kept exactly (fractional tons), so `expected_provisions_tons` is what is eaten before the last leg sets out (no hazards) and `safe_provisions_tons` also survives the worst storm on any leg (most storms take far less; pirates who let a ship go can take more). Buy the shortfall against the ship's `stores.provisions_tons`, rounded up to whole tons.

Contributions from all companies stack. Aggregates only: sponsors are never named.
